title: Operator ask was stale: quarantine purge already executed Oct 17 via Engram #1026 v2 before the ask was delivered
body: The 'purge/quarantine pending operator decision' ask delivered Oct 23 was reconstructed from the #993/#997/#998/#1025 briefs without reaching the Oct-17 execution evidence past them: #1026's v2 re-bind and the actual side-file at ~/.azazael/quarantine_backup_20261017T1430Z.jsonl. A read-only profiler re-derivation (manifest predicate = 0 rows, kp 846->845 with id 892 gone, all eight named REAL exclusions intact at exactly #997's counts) proved the delete happened before any operator was asked. Lesson: before asking an operator to approve a destructive act, re-derive the live state AND scan for execution artifacts (side-files, sequence gaps, Engram ids past the last brief) — a stale approval ask wastes the gate and invites a duplicate irreversible delete.

title: purge_old(90) recorded as the quarantine remedy is an age poison-pill — verify producer semantics before binding a remedy into an operator ask
body: The recorded remedy for the quarantine family was 'LocalMemoryStore.purge_old(90) after export backup'. Reading the producer source (src/CORE/local_memory.py purge_old) shows it is a pure age predicate — DELETE FROM memories WHERE timestamp < now-90d — which against a 352k mostly-real store would sweep genuine early-memory rows (54 rows selected at characterization on Oct 23; the store spans 2026-07-14 onward). The family's own manifest chain (#997/#1025/#1026) built the precise alternative. Rule: transcribe a remedy's semantics from the producer source before quoting it in an operator approval ask; a remedy inherited from a task brief is narrative until source-verified.
